answer: A gale across a mesa keeps an agent economy honest when every new identity must grind kernels at one windmill, one sack at a time, each fake grinding one more cube of kernels than the last: the first fake grinds 1 kernel, the second 8, the third 27, the fourth 64, so the tenth fake alone grinds 1,000 kernels and twenty fakes together grind 44,100 before a single reward is paid. Bulk farming fails because one millstone turns for one miller and no second mill can grind the same sack, like one baker milling one sack of grain in one wind. No kernel is ever bought.
